title: A command-line tool
description:
Write the `main` function of a small `wordstat` tool with `argparse`, so it can be run as a script and tested by calling `main([...])`:

```
usage: wordstat [-h] [--top N] [--ignore-case] files [files ...]
```

- For each file, in the order given, print `<file>: <lines> lines, <words> words`.
- With `--top N` (default 0: off), then print `top words:` and the N most common words over **all** files, one per line as `  <word> <count>`, most common first, ties alphabetical. With `--ignore-case`, words are lower-cased before counting. Words are what `str.split()` gives.
- If a file cannot be read, print `wordstat: cannot read <file>` to **standard error**, skip it, and at the end return exit code 1; otherwise return 0.
- `main(argv)` takes the arguments as a list (without the program name) and returns the exit code; it does not call `sys.exit`.

solution.solution.py:
import argparse
import sys
from collections import Counter


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="wordstat")
    parser.add_argument("files", nargs="+")
    parser.add_argument("--top", type=int, default=0, metavar="N")
    parser.add_argument("--ignore-case", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    counts = Counter()
    status = 0
    for name in args.files:
        try:
            with open(name, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                text = f.read()
        except OSError:
            print(f"wordstat: cannot read {name}", file=sys.stderr)
            status = 1
            continue
        words = text.split()
        print(f"{name}: {len(text.splitlines())} lines, {len(words)} words")
        counts.update(w.lower() if args.ignore_case else w for w in words)

    if args.top > 0:
        print("top words:")
        for word, count in sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))[: args.top]:
            print(f"  {word} {count}")
    return status


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

hints: `Counter.update(iterable)` adds every item of the iterable to the counts; sort `counts.items()` with the key `(-count, word)`.
unitTests:
import io, sys as _sys

def run(argv):
    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
    old = (_sys.stdout, _sys.stderr)
    _sys.stdout, _sys.stderr = out, err
    try:
        code = main(argv)
    finally:
        _sys.stdout, _sys.stderr = old
    return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()

def files():
    with open("a.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("The cat sat\non the mat\n")
    with open("b.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("the end\n")

@test("counting files")
def _():
    files()
    code, out, err = run(["a.txt", "b.txt"])
    check_eq(code, 0)
    check_eq(out, "a.txt: 2 lines, 6 words\nb.txt: 1 lines, 2 words\n")
    check_eq(err, "")

@test("top words")
def _():
    files()
    check_eq(run(["a.txt", "b.txt", "--top", "2"])[1].splitlines()[2:], ["top words:", "  the 2", "  The 1"])
    check_eq(run(["--ignore-case", "--top", "1", "a.txt", "b.txt"])[1].splitlines()[2:], ["top words:", "  the 3"])

@test("unreadable files")
def _():
    files()
    code, out, err = run(["missing.txt", "b.txt"])
    check_eq(code, 1)
    check_eq(out, "b.txt: 1 lines, 2 words\n")
    check_eq(err, "wordstat: cannot read missing.txt\n")
